text:
PACKET-03: BLIND FIRST READING (UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING)

Exposure statement
- Nothing in my context proposed an identification or a reading of this text. This is a blind reading.
- What I did beyond the rules: I ran a directory listing of the packet folder (to enumerate the image files) and a `sips` call to get pixel dimensions, so I could tell overviews from tiles. I did not open packet.json or anything outside the packet. I made no web, catalogue or edition lookups.
- Visible on the leaf (observation only, not an identification of the work): image-001/002 top left has a modern pencil shelfmark "Fragm. lat. 56" and an oval library stamp reading "UNIVERSITÄTS- / BIBLIOTHEK / LEIPZIG". Image-015/020 left margin has a pencil "<56>", and image-015/017 top right has a modern "2".

====================================================================
1. LAYOUT SURVEY (images only)
====================================================================
The packet holds four faces. Each has one reduced overview and six overlapping native tiles:
  Face A: overview image-001; tiles 002 (col a top), 003 (col b top), 004 (col a middle), 005 (col b middle), 006 (col a bottom), 007 (col b bottom)
  Face B: overview image-008; tiles 009-014 in the same order
  Face C: overview image-015; tiles 016-021 in the same order
  Face D: overview image-022; tiles 023-028 in the same order
Faces C and D are narrower overviews (1257 px wide), and their outer margins look trimmed or damaged. I cannot tell from the images which faces are recto and verso of the same leaf.

Common features, observed:
- Upright orientation, two columns of about 50-55 lines, ruled in drypoint or plummet. Gothic cursive/semi-cursive book hand with very heavy abbreviation, brown ink.
- Line-initial capital ascenders are extended into the top margin as tall flourished strokes (cadels) above the first line of each column on all faces.
- Throughout, many short phrases are underlined in the ink of the text. These underlined phrases recur at short intervals and are often followed by "i(d est)" or "q(uasi) d(icat)" glosses. Interpretation (tentative): underlined = quoted lemmata of a base text, with the unmarked prose as commentary. Recurrent markers include "legat(ur) l(itte)ra sic", "Tunc recapitulat", "postq(uam) o(stendi)t ... h(ic) o(stendit)", "p(rim)a f(acit) q(uod) d(icit)" and "s(ecundu)m" and "no(ta)/Sciendum" type openers ("Sc(ien)d(u)m q(uod)", written "flo^d"-like).
- Larger display-script openings, observed:
    Face A col a line 1: "Speculans enim." (enlarged gothic, not underlined).
    Face A col b, lower part: "Nunc autem." (enlarged, indented), opening a new section.
    Face D col b, lower part: a large two-line initial (a pen-drawn Q/O form with a long descending tail) followed by enlarged "[Q]uod autem non sit" (or similar), opening a new section.
    Face B col a about line 11 (image-009): "Dicendum autem" in a larger, darker script mid-line.
    Face C col b (image-017 line 21): "Dubitat(?) ad(?)" underlined at the start of a line.
- Marginalia: Face A col b upper margin has a faint later note "[..] dut(?) abut(?) II". There is a small marginal "Ϝ"/"ff"-like sign beside col b in the middle (image-003 right edge) and a circled note "ute(?)" beside col b (image-005 right edge). Face A lower margin under col a holds a faint line "[..] (et) altera[..] .. q(ui) [..] priuate(?) disp(ositi)o(n)es" (catchword or note; uncertain). Face B upper right has a faint "[.]lo^a(?) II"; the col a/col b gutter of Face B has a small "sic(?)". Face B lower margin under col a has a faint note and one under col b; illegible at overview scale. Face C top centre has "[..]tia" (possibly a running word; I read the letters only). Face C left margin has an arrow-like mark before image-020 line 15.
- Damage: holes in Face A col a (image-004 line 14) and Face A col b (image-003 line 5; image-007 lower right, about 3 lines). Face B has a hole at image-012 line 15 and a loss at image-013 lower left (about 3 lines). Face C has a large torn hole in col b mid-lower (image-019 lines 8-11, about 4 lines lost at line ends), a hole at image-021 lines 11-12, and a large round hole at image-021 lines 16-20 (mid-line loss). Face D has a torn edge in col a (image-025 lines 9-12, line beginnings lost), small holes, and a large round hole at the foot of col a (image-027 lines 17-20). The script is faded in parts of Face C col a (lower half) and Face D col a (outer margin browned).

Selected areas:
- Face A: col a lines 1-15 (image-002); col b lines 1-13 (image-003); col b "Nunc autem" section (image-007, lines 15-26).
- Face B: col a lines 1-12 (image-009); col b lines 1-12 (image-010).
- Face C: col a lines 1-10 (image-016); col b lines 1-12 and the "Dubitat" lines (image-017).
- Face D: col b lines 1-12 (image-024); col b "Quod autem" section (image-028, lines 1-12).
Left unread: most of the middles and bottoms of every column, apart from scattered words. Face C col a lower half (image-018/020) and Face D col a (image-023/025/027) were skimmed but not transcribed; they are faded and heavily abbreviated.

Conventions: (..) is a proposed expansion; "word?" is an uncertain reading; [illegible] means not read; [hole] means physical loss; _..._ marks text underlined in the MS. Line numbers count text lines from the top of the named tile. Overlapping tiles repeat lines; I transcribe each line once, from the tile named.
Caveat: the abbreviation system is dense. Many of my expansions are guesses at the system, not secure readings. Treat every expansion as provisional.

- The hand is a small, very heavily abbreviated cursive. At this resolution a large share of the abbreviation marks cannot be resolved. Most expansions are hypotheses about the system, not secure readings. The secure items are the display words "Speculans enim", "Nunc autem", "Dicendum autem" and "Quod autem non sit"; the formulae "legatur littera sic", "Tunc recapitulat", "postquam ostendit ... hic ostendit" and "prima facit quod dicit"; and recurrent content words (sensus, sensibile, actu/potentia, alterari, addiscere, color, uisus, auditus, odor/olfactus, aer, sonus, tactus/tangibilia, organum).
- Column order within each face is clear (a then b). The order of the four faces relative to one another is unknown from the images.
- Overlap: tiles 002/004/006 (and their counterparts) overlap by about 4-6 lines. I took each line once from the tile named.
- Physical losses (holes and the torn edge) affect Face A col b about lines 5-6 and 15-17 (image-003/007); Face B col a line 5 (image-009) and lower left (image-013); Face C col b mid-lower (image-019, about 4 lines) and foot (image-021); Face D col a lines 9-12 (image-025) and foot (image-027).
- For checkable matching I recommend: (1) higher-magnification crops, about 2x native, of Face A col a lines 1-15 and Face D col b lines 1-12 (image-028); (2) a raking-light or enhanced image of the faded lower half of Face C col a (image-018/020) and of Face D col a; (3) a crop of the lower-margin notes on Faces A and B and the top-margin notes on Faces A, B and C.
